def: extremely hungry
example: By the time I got to school I was starving.

def: completely wet, right through your clothes
example: A van drove through a puddle and soaked me.

def: extremely cold
example: It was freezing outside and raining hard.

def: so tired that you can hardly move
example: By four o'clock I was exhausted.

def: extremely angry
example: I was still furious with my alarm clock.

def: happy because something bad is finally over
example: I was relieved that the day was over.

def: so shocked that you cannot react
example: I stood there, absolutely stunned.

def: uncomfortable and embarrassing
example: There was an awkward silence in the class.

def: to look at something very quickly
example: He glanced at me over his glasses and said nothing.

def: to move somewhere in a big hurry
example: I grabbed my clothes and rushed out.

def: to slide by accident and almost fall
example: I slipped on the corridor floor.

def: to take something suddenly with your hand
example: She grabbed her bag and ran.

def: to suddenly feel so frightened that you cannot think
example: I woke up at eight and panicked.

def: to suddenly understand something
example: I didn't realise that it was raining.

def: to see or hear something without looking for it
example: Nobody noticed that I was late.

def: to succeed in doing something difficult
example: I managed to catch the last bus.

def: to be somewhere or in a situation you did not plan
example: I ended up walking forty minutes in the rain.

def: to meet somebody by chance
example: At lunchtime I ran into Daria.

def: quickly and unexpectedly
example: I was reading when suddenly the lights went out.

def: at the same time, in another place or situation
example: The bus, meanwhile, went past without stopping.

def: in the end, after a long time
example: We waited forty minutes and eventually a taxi arrived.

def: at once, without any delay
example: She saw the smoke and immediately called her father.

def: it is fortunate that…
example: Luckily, nobody was hurt.

def: used to say that something had already happened when another thing happened
example: By the time I got to school, the lesson had started.
